facts.statement: The genus Dawndraco was named by Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2010.
facts.quote: Dawndraco was named by Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2010.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Dawndraco kanzai.
facts.quote: The type species is Dawndraco kanzai.

facts.statement: The generic name Dawndraco combines the Dawn deity of the Iroquois with the Latin word for dragon.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Dawn deity of the Iroquois with a Latin draco, "dragon".

facts.statement: The specific name kanzai refers to the Kanza tribe of Kansas.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Kanza tribe of Kansas.

facts.statement: The genus is based on holotype specimen UALVP 24238, a partial skeleton with an almost complete skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: Dawndraco is based on the holotype specimen UALVP 24238, a partial skeleton including an almost complete skull and lower jaws.

facts.statement: The fossil was recovered in 1974 by Richard C. Fox and Allen Lindoe from the Niobrara Formation in Utica, Kansas.
facts.quote: It was recovered in 1974 by Richard C. Fox and Allen Lindoe from rocks of the lower part of the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation in Utica, Kansas.

facts.statement: The rocks containing the fossil date to the late Coniacian or early Santonian stage, approximately 86 million years ago.
facts.quote: These rocks date to the late Coniacian or early Santonian stage, about 86 million years ago.

facts.statement: Kellner assigned Dawndraco to the family Pteranodontidae.
facts.quote: 'Dawndraco' was assigned by Kellner to the Pteranodontidae.

facts.statement: Martin-Silverstone et al. argued that the taxonomic characterizations of Dawndraco were suspect and that the stratigraphic arguments used to distinguish it were questionable.
facts.quote: They showed that its taxonomic characterisations were suspect or erroneous, and that stratigraphic arguments used to further distinguish 'D. kanzai from other pteranodontids were questionable when compared to the geologic ranges of other Smoky Hill Chalk species.

facts.statement: Martin-Silverstone et al. interpreted the specimen as a small, immature individual of the larger male size class of Pteranodon sternbergi.
facts.quote: They concluded that UALVP 24238 is better interpreted as a small (not fully osteologically mature) individual of the larger size-class (male) of Pteranodon sternbergi.

facts.statement: The time range for Dawndraco is from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dawndraco belongs to the family Pteranodontidae.
The authority for the genus Dawndraco is Kellner, 2010.

rejected.quote: A unique trait is that the snout does not strongly taper anteriorly as with Pteranodon, the upper and lower margins running almost parallel instead.

rejected.quote: Dawndraco is a controversial genus of pteranodontid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. It is likely synonymous with the contemporary pteranodontid Geosternbergia.
